LingoDeer is honestly one of the best apps for learning Korean! 🇰🇷 I really like how it teaches you step by step instead of just throwing random words at you. The lessons are easy to understand, and the explanations actually help you understand WHY Korean works the way it does.

reviews.title: Great Tool for Japanese
reviews.text: As with any language APP, I don’t think it’s realistic to think LingoDeer will get you to a fluent level by itself, but it is a great foundation to get started. The recent upgrades including AI mistake explanation and literal translations are super helpful. I love the videos with real people speaking. The SRS and review tools are helpful. If you want to start Japanese this is a great way to do it. Supplement the app with beginner podcast and find other ways to immerse yourself and practice writing and recall. For future improvements I’d love more cross hiragana, katakana, and kanji quizzes and learning tools. I also think more stories for each lesson with transcripts to review would also be helpful. Lastly, find a way to make the gems and experience points to actually mean something…maybe credits or real value for learning tools, online lessons, etc. For dedicated learners, I’m not sure the gems mean anything and they will keep coming back to learn anyways.  Consider embedding your own beginner podcasts into the app or linking to LingoDeer podcasts for beginners so we don’t have to go to other outlets and hunt for immersion opportunities. Bottom line, the app is really helpful for people who know nothing about Japanese and want to learn. I’ve had a lot of fun with it. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: It is useful
reviews.text: I have been using Lingodeer for a year now.  I spend between 20 minutes to 3 hours a day, depending on what free time I have.  I can make basic sentences and can read a very basic children's book.  My listening skills are developing, I can make out words if the speaker does not speak fast.  The benefit of this software depends on the effort you put in.  It will not deposit the knowledge just by clicking and repeating, you have to actually spend time committing rules and vocab to memory. It is hard and repetitive work.  The grammar is not explained very well, but you will see a pattern and then Google helps tremendously to determine why the translation looks like it does with the conjugations used.  I am happy using LingoDeer.  I use it as the core of my studies and then I have added the Genki Books, another piece of software to learn Kanji and Google to explain the grammar. Yes, I would recommend LingoDeer, it provides a good structure to learning. Also, the support staff are really good when you might have a problem.

reviews.title: Switching Between Formal Polite and Informal Polite
reviews.text: Just when I thought I was gaining an understanding of Korean formal polite diction (니다 endings) the curriculum switched over to Korean informal polite (어요 endings) with a new set of rules (!!). Now I am uncertain which format to use and how the new format will impact what I have already learned, and my trip to Korea is coming up. If I had a preference, I would want the app to stay with Korean formal polite (or vice-versa) and not switch over to the other format until I had gained a higher level of proficiency and could make the choice myself on when to switch. I am not very good at the language, but was getting better. The switch to the new format makes it harder. I also think it would be helpful to have an elective track of useful Korean travel phrases that could be reviewed before traveling, vs. the sometimes challenging mental exercises your normal Korean curriculum offers (e.g., “Today my grandmother said she does not like blue dresses.”) That random complexity of taught sentence structure was the main reason I dropped Duolingo.

reviews.title: Great help
reviews.text:
In conjunction with a tutor, I’ve been using this app to study Japanese for the last 4 years and am finally reaching the end of the learning path. It’s been really helpful and I appreciate the improvements I’ve seen over that time. I’m only 1/3 of the way through the “fluent” section, so I have more to work on.

I traveled to japan after year 2 and was able to communicate in the stores and museums. I’d feel much more comfortable now, even though I’m still just a beginner. 

One thing I would have appreciated was a suggestion on how to study using the app. I never knew when to incorporate the LingoDeer+ app, so I’m very behind there. I’d also love to do some review without having to go back through the app. There’s some concepts I’m weak in and I can’t remember where to find them again. 

The fluent section feels a little backwards to me. There was a story of a mom and son and the son was being fairly incompetent about taking care of the house while the mom was gone. But I read it in the order it was presented to me and it was backwards. So I read the end, then the mom’s frustration, then mom leaving and giving instructions, it was confusing for a bit. 

I have recommended this to friends and I look forward to continued improvements.
